questions.stem: Find terminal speed for mass 1 kg, drag 0.5 kg/s, g=9.81 in m/s.
questions.explanation: v_t = mg/b. The tempting error is to divide b by mg.

questions.subject: PHYSICS_MECHANICS
questions.topic: Ballistic coefficient from a projectile's dimensions
questions.stem: A design brief reduces cross-sectional area; what happens to ballistic coefficient?

options.text: It increases because less area means less drag sensitivity.
It decreases because area is in numerator.
It stays the same because mass unchanged.
It halves because area halves.

questions.explanation: Smaller area raises BC. The tempting error is to treat area as numerator.

questions.subject: PHYSICS_MECHANICS
questions.topic: Reading a range table against launch angle
questions.stem: Given peak range 100 m at 45 deg, find range at 30 deg in metres.
questions.explanation: Range at 30 deg is sin 60 times peak scaling; 86.6 m. The tempting error is to halve the peak.

questions.subject: PHYSICS_MECHANICS
questions.topic: Scaling of flight time with launch speed
questions.stem: Explain why flight time is independent of mass in ideal projectile motion.

answer.exemplar: Acceleration due to gravity is independent of mass, and time of flight depends only on vertical velocity and g.

questions.explanation: g is mass-independent. The tempting wrong idea is that heavier projectiles fall faster.

questions.topic: Expression for range from the trajectory equation
questions.stem: Compute range for v=40 m/s, theta=25 degrees in metres (g=9.81).
questions.explanation: R = v^2 sin 50 / g. The tempting error is to use sin 25.
